newsitem.title: USA: Domestic crudes trade slightly weaker in U.S. Gulf.
newsitem.headline: Domestic crudes trade slightly weaker in U.S. Gulf.

text.p: Domestic crude grade barrels in the U.S. Gulf weakened Friday afternoon against a softer outright price for benchmark July West Texas Intermediate/Cushing.
Traders said refiners were still not actively seeking grade barrels, but there were some signs of life.
The market featured a strong July Exchange for Physical (EFP) sector, which talked at 13-15 cents over July futures.

Traders noted, however, that the premium held by EFPs seems to have worked its way into the futures value. July NYMEX was trading around 15 cents weaker at $20.75-85 a barrel, and held a 13 cents discount to August NYMEX.
"I think the EFP price is well ground in the NYMEX price. I don't think we'd see July/August at the discount without the EFPs so strong," said a Gulf cash dealer.

Fundamentals for grade barrels were a bit bearish, pushing Light Louisiana Sweet/St. James to sell at discounts of 14 and 15 cents to July cash WTI. The most volume was sold at the 15 cents level, putting LLS at the weaker end of Thursday's trading range.
Trade sources said LLS barrels were being shoved into inventory, pressuring values. At the same time, unsold offshore sour barrels were also weighing on differentials.
"There seems to be some hangover from Mars," said a trader, noting barrels from Shell's deepwater Gulf field were not snapped-up immediately.
Other trades were confirmed for Heavy Louisiana Sweet/Empire at 60 cents under July WTI, and Eugene Island at minus $1.60.
